minutes.headline: Planning Board could not act on a common driveway for lack of a quorum; long debate on draft special event permit rules
minutes.summary: The board could not act on a common driveway request at 205 Sunset Lane because one member was recused, so it was continued to April 8. Most of the meeting was a long discussion, with many residents speaking, of the Board of Selectmen's draft special event permit policy and a Holman Street resident's request about events. The board voted to support a DLTA application for an ADA transition plan, approved several sets of minutes, tabled the building reuse item, and heard a proposed anti-segmentation change to the cluster bylaw.

public_comment.topic: Asked for guidance and meetings with town departments on three special events on his property and shared citizen petition documents.
Asked whether department-head feedback on the three events had been returned to the applicant.
Asked why the discussion was held given a cease and desist letter sent to the applicant.
Questioned why an applicant who held events documented as illegal would get a permit or variance.
The applicant disputed the figure of 29 events and defended a garden club visit.
Said the policy seems aimed at one property, urged protecting residential character and allowing public-land events.
Asked that the limit of four events per year be cut to two.
Said definitions are too vague; focus on multi-day events.
Said advertised events bring outsiders and overnight camping into a quiet neighborhood.
Said residential property is typically not open to the public.
Asked for guidance on protecting large open parcels.
Said tents are a fire department matter and jurisdiction needs sorting before a hearing.

budget_items.what_was_said: The land use director said it costs the community about five thousand dollars and did not recommend it now.

A state grant could be matched one-to-one with capital funds sought at Town Meeting.
A member said cleanup charges should be itemized in advance.

Land use director and the applicant to arrange a meeting with relevant town departments on the proposed events.
A board member was nominated for the land acquisition committee.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board could not act on the common driveway at 205 Sunset Lane because a recusal left it without a quorum, so it was continued to April 8.
Most of the meeting was spent on the Selectmen's draft special event permit policy, with many residents speaking; the board gave feedback to the Selectmen.
The board voted to table the building reuse item to its next meeting.
The board voted to support a DLTA request for an ADA transition plan and to send a letter of support.
A proposed anti-segmentation change to the cluster bylaw will be discussed April 8, with the land use director to email the Framingham language.

why_it_matters: The special event policy would set how often, and under what conditions, events can be held on residential and open land, which affects neighbors and property owners in town.
The ADA transition plan request and a possible master plan grant, which could be matched with capital funds sought at Town Meeting, are items that could later come before voters as spending.
